evidence.quote: at our meeting later this month, the Committee will evaluate whether employment and inflation are continuing to evolve in line with our expectations, in which case a further adjustment of the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate.
the process of scaling back accommodation likely will not be as slow as it was in 2015 and 2016.
The economy has essentially met the employment portion of our mandate and inflation is moving closer to our 2 percent objective.
The Committee currently assesses that the risks to the outlook are roughly balanced.
Core PCE inflation--which excludes volatile energy and food prices and, therefore, tends to be a better indicator of future inflation--has been running near 1-3/4 percent.

I currently see no evidence that the Federal Reserve has fallen behind the curve, and I therefore continue to have confidence in our judgment that a gradual removal of accommodation is likely to be appropriate.

parsed.rationale: The speech signals a likely rate hike at the upcoming meeting and a faster pace of removing accommodation than in 2015-16, citing a labor market at maximum employment. It tempers this with gradualism, balanced risks, and an assessment that inflation is still somewhat below target and not behind the curve.
